verses.text: From the blue, purple, and red yarn they made woven clothes for serving in the Holy Place. They also made the holy clothes for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Bezalel made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
They hammered the gold into thin sheets and cut it into threads, to weave into the blue, purple, and red yarn and the fine linen, the work of a skilled worker.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, fastened to its two corners, so that it could be tied together.
Its skilfully woven belt was made the same way and was one piece with it, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They set the onyx stones in gold settings and carved on them the names of the sons of Israel, the way a jeweller carves a seal.
Then they fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as stones to remind God of the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the chest piece, the work of a skilled worker, like the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, and red yarn, and fine twisted linen.
It was square, folded double, about twenty-three centimetres long and twenty-three centimetres wide.
They put four rows of precious stones on it. In the first row was a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl.
In the second row was a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald.
In the third row was a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst.
In the fourth row was a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They were set in gold settings.
There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each stone was carved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the chest piece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like a rope.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to the two upper corners of the chest piece.
They fastened the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the chest piece.
They fastened the other ends of the chains to the two settings, and attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and fastened them to the other two corners of the chest piece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and fastened them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to the seam just above its woven belt.

They tied the rings of the chest piece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that the chest piece sat above the woven belt and did not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod, woven all of blue cloth.
There was an opening in the middle of the robe like a collar, with a woven edge around the opening so that it would not tear.
Around the bottom hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple, and red yarn and twisted linen.
They made bells of pure gold and put them between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe.
A bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, went all around the hem of the robe to be worn for serving as priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
For Aaron and his sons they made shirts woven from fine linen,
and the turban of fine linen, the linen caps, and the underwear of fine twisted linen.
The sash was made of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and red yarn, the work of someone who sews beautiful patterns, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate, the holy crown, out of pure gold, and carved on it like a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
They tied a blue cord to it to fasten it on the turban, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work on the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting, was finished. The people of Israel did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then they brought the holy tent to Moses: the tent and all its furniture, its hooks, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the curtain that hides the ark;
the ark of the covenant with its poles and its cover;
the table with all its tools and the special bread;
the pure gold lampstand with its row of lamps and all its tools, and the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the sweet-smelling incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grate, its poles and all its tools, and the washing bowl with its stand;
the curtains of the courtyard with their posts and bases, the screen for the entrance to the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the tools for the work of the holy tent, the Tent of Meeting;
and the woven clothes for serving in the Holy Place, both the holy clothes for Aaron the priest and the clothes for his sons when they serve as priests.
The people of Israel had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses looked over all the work and saw that they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
